S1.rationale: The supported operational BaseAgent and bundled SWE reference agent already perform model-directed task and tool work and absorb tool/test results. This assessment alone supplies no specific task-execution failure requiring a separate S1 product intervention.

S2.rationale: The standard evolution loop binds one BaseAgent, with task batching and process isolation reflecting repeated episodes rather than two interacting continuing S1 divisions. There is no evidenced native inter-worker disturbance to repair by adding an S2 arbiter.

S3.rationale: EvolutionLoop scheduling, limits, historical observations and convergence gates manage configured cycles; the default adaptation actor governs future workspace changes, not a separate live portfolio of S1 obligations. No bounded current-resource management problem is substantiated.

S3*.rationale: BenchmarkAdapter.evaluate independently scores operational trajectories and returns Feedback under constructor-selected criteria, while no first-party common independent audit owner exists. The assessment provides no concrete false-pass incident or native testing defect justifying an additional evaluator patch.

S4.rationale: The default AEvolveEngine owns prospective persistent mutations after benchmark feedback (S4=A). During independent current-code checking, pre-existing issue #28 exposed a native conditional safety concern: compile-only candidate validation versus in-process exec_module of mutable harness.py. This mechanism was NOT diagnosed by the Index; linked candidate is ASSESSMENT_INFORMED, not a strict S4 assessment-derived finding.

S5.rationale: The manifest and EvolveConfig enforce developer/operator-selected writable layers and identity constraints, not a first-party ultimate-policy decision loop. No product-specific request or evidence supports automatically adding an S5 authority to this evolution tool.
